{{short description|American mathematician}}

'''Christine Guenther''' is an American mathematician known for her research on the [[differential geometry]] of [[manifold]]s, including the [[Ricci flow]]. She is a distinguished professor of mathematics at [[Pacific University]].{{r|pac}}

Guenther graduated from [[Stanford University]] in 1989 with a bachelor's degree in music. After earning a master's degree in mathematics in 1993 from the [[University of Washington]],{{r|pac}} she completed her Ph.D. in 1998 at the [[University of Oregon]], under the supervision of [[James A. Isenberg]].{{r|pac|mgp}}
She joined the Pacific University faculty in 1988 and became a Distinguished University Professor at Pacific University in 2016.{{r|presents}}

She is a co-author of the four-volume book series ''Ricci Flow: Techniques and Applications'' (American Mathematical Society, 2007, 2008, 2010, and 2015){{r|flow}}
and of ''[[Extrinsic Geometric Flows]]'' ([[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] 206, 2020).{{r|xgf}}
